title: World Cup 2026 pool: market-anchored Bayesian simulation with a rank objective
pitch: A daily decision system that picks scores to maximize the probability of finishing first, not expected points. It finished 1st with a 13-point lead going into the final.
bullets: Goal model: Dixon-Coles with host advantage. Shape parameters fitted once with NumPyro NUTS on 15,636 international matches; team strengths re-anchored to the betting market every day by Shin de-vigging 1X2 and totals odds and inverting them with a KL-minimizing solver in JAX. The market is the prior; no edge is claimed over it.
Simulation: 500,000 full-tournament scenarios per night (groups, best-thirds matching over all 495 combinations, bracket) with a shared strength draw per scenario for cross-match correlation.

Rivals: each of 32 opponents gets a latent style (sharpness, favourite bias, high-score bias, contrarianism) with hierarchical partial pooling, inferred only from their leaderboard deltas by convolving per-match score laws. Their picks were never observed.

Optimizer: Rao-Blackwellized estimate of P(win) with common random numbers and coordinate ascent. The resulting value curve made batches risk-seeking when behind and risk-averse when ahead without hard-coding either.

Results: exact-score rate 18.5% (12 of 65 comparable matches) vs 8.75% for the average rival. Ex-ante P(win) on day one was 0.40 against a 1/32 baseline. Counterfactual on the same 96 picks, 90-minute scoreline points only: this optimizer 112, max-expected-points 104, modal picks 101. Calibration against Bet365 correct-score odds was within noise (n = 25) and is reported as such.

Stack: Python 3.12, JAX, NumPyro, DuckDB and Parquet, Typer CLI, FastAPI, Next.js, Streamlit; about 8,500 lines, 60 tests, 5 LaTeX specification documents and 7 architecture decision records. Everything ran on CPU on a laptop.

title: HackICN 2025: fast power-grid topology reduction
context: 2nd place. Team Sistemas Cyberdyne, Instituto de Ciencias Nucleares, UNAM. Sponsored by Bravos Energía and Huawei; 240+ applications.
pitch: Reduce Mexico's transmission-grid graph so power-flow sensitivities compute faster while critical buses and lines are preserved.
bullets: Distribution factors scale as O(n^3): doubling the grid means eight times the compute.
Pipeline: mark critical nodes and lines, collapse parallel branches, prune radial leaves, eliminate series buses.
Reduction factor 0.46 in 1.7 seconds; distribution-factor computation went from 63 s to 24 s, about 2.6x faster.

title: From Lotka-Volterra to chaos in food chains
context: Dynamical Systems II, ITAM. With Emilio Leguizamo.
pitch: Qualitative and numerical analysis of predator-prey models, from the conservative two-species case to a chaotic three-species chain.
bullets: Lotka-Volterra: Hartman-Grobman at the saddle, a Lyapunov function built from the first integral at the non-hyperbolic center, and Poincare-Bendixson to show every interior orbit is periodic. Adding a logistic term with epsilon = 0.15 turns the center into a stable focus, which exhibits the model's structural instability.

Rosenzweig-MacArthur: Holling type II response and a Hopf bifurcation at carrying capacity K of about 4.67 (the paradox of enrichment), verified numerically with a limit cycle of period about 17.4 at K = 6.

Hastings-Powell in 3D: the teacup strange attractor, a period-doubling cascade whose ratios approach Feigenbaum's constant, a largest Lyapunov exponent of 0.0064 (plus or minus 0.0002) by Benettin's algorithm, and a Poincare section with 612 points consistent with dimension about 2.07.
Numerics with scipy RK45 at rtol 1e-10; the conserved quantity drifted less than 7.4e-11 over the run.

title: HitMonsters: load-testing a TCP and pub/sub multiplayer game
pitch: A Java multiplayer game with TCP authentication and hits and an ActiveMQ topic for monster spawns, stress-tested from 50 to 500 concurrent clients.
bullets: Hit races resolved with compareAndSet so exactly one player scores; state in a ConcurrentHashMap; 4 s heartbeat with 8 s timeout to detect crashed clients.
Stress harness: 50 to 500 clients, 10 repetitions each, simulated reaction times, 5% abrupt disconnects with reconnection.
Hit success stayed at or above 99.5% at every load; registration success collapsed to 26.8% at 350 clients because of the thread-per-connection model and the socket backlog, not TCP.
The pub/sub layer's temporal decoupling kept the game path robust; the proposed fix for registration is a bounded thread pool.

title: Optimal racing line with a from-scratch L-BFGS trust-region solver
context: Applied Analysis, ITAM. With Martín Fabre and Eduardo García.
pitch: Minimize lap time on real Formula 1 circuit geometry by optimizing lateral position and speed together, with vehicle limits as soft penalties.
bullets: Centrelines from open circuit GeoJSON, projected and resampled every 30 m on a 12 m wide track; decision vector of sigmoid lateral offsets plus segment speeds.
Objective: total time plus exponential penalties for speed, longitudinal acceleration (10 m/s^2), minimum turning radius (10 m) and lateral acceleration (mu = 1.7).
Solver: limited-memory BFGS (m = 5, two-loop recursion) inside a simplified trust region, finite-difference gradients, 100 iterations.
Lap times: Monza 159.1 s, Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez 133.6 s, roughly 50 to 100% above F1 records, which the 30 m discretization and simplified physics explain.
